perspective:
From Jose Castillo’s perspective:

- I work with Patricia at the community bank, where I help with maintenance and repairs. She’s a bank teller there.
- I’d noticed she seemed more withdrawn and less vibrant than usual. When I asked if she was okay, she said it was “nothing really, just some personal stuff” and thanked me for asking. I offered to listen if she ever wanted to talk, and she said she appreciated that.
- During a lunch break, I overheard her on the phone sounding worried about bills and financial commitments. I told her I’d been reading about financial planning and offered to discuss it with her. She said that could be helpful and that she’d been overwhelmed with her bills lately. I suggested we could look at budgeting tips together, and she said she’d take me up on it soon.
- Afterward, I worried I might have overstepped by bringing up finances, so I told Patricia I wanted to help, not pry. She said she didn’t see it as prying and was grateful for the offer. I assured her I respected her privacy and just wanted to support her as a friend. She said it meant a lot and that it was good to know she had someone to turn to.
- After that conversation, I sensed she appreciated my concern but seemed to prefer handling things privately. I checked in with her again, and she said everything was all good and she was planning a quiet weekend at home. I said I’d probably relax and read, and reminded her she could reach out if she needed anything or just wanted to chat. She thanked me and said she’d keep that in mind.
- I’ve kept checking in with her at work. I told her she could let me know if she needed help with anything, even just grabbing a coffee. She said she was busy but handling it, thanked me for checking in, and said it was really great to have my support. I said anytime, and that we’re all there to help each other out.
final_response:
From Jose’s perspective, he first offered to listen and be supportive when Patricia seemed withdrawn. Later, after overhearing her financial worries, he offered financial planning advice. So his intention shifted from offering general support to offering financial advice.

ANSWER: c
